blogs.title: Semaglutide Unexpected: When a Weight‑Loss Drug Triggers Immune‑Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
blogs.description: A case‑based review of a 60‑year‑old woman who developed progressive proximal weakness and a 12‑fold rise in CK four months after a single semaglutide dose. We outline the clinical suspicion, the temporal pattern that sets it apart from classical statin‑induced myopathy or reversible rhabdomyolysis, and the key red‑flags that should prompt early myopathy work‑up.

blogs.title: Rhabdo or Autoimmunity? Decoding CK Dynamics in Drug‑Induced Myopathies
blogs.description: An educational guide to interpreting creatinine kinase trajectories, MRI findings, and EMG patterns when a patient presents with acute CK elevation versus a gradual rise over weeks. The article stresses why a slow, persistent increase, coupled with proximal weakness and dysphagia, points to immune‑mediated necrosis rather than pure drug toxicity.

blogs.title: Seronegative IMNM: How to Diagnose and Treat When Classic Autoantibodies Fail
blogs.description: Detailing the diagnostic algorithm for immune‑mediated necrotizing myopathy when HMGCR and SRP antibodies are absent—highlighting the role of muscle biopsy, inflammatory markers, and imaging. The post also discusses differential diagnosis, the significance of isolated SS‑B positivity, and strategies to distinguish drug‑induced from idiopathic disease.

blogs.title: High‑Dose Steroids, IVIG, and the Art of Tapering: Managing a GLP‑1‑Induced Myopathy
blogs.description: A practical treatment roadmap for clinicians facing drug‑induced IMNM, including induction therapy with pulse methylprednisolone, oral prednisone taper, the rationale for IVIG, and monitoring for relapse. It also addresses infection risk and circumstances where a brief course may suffice.

blogs.title: From Semaglutide to Safety Signals: The Role of Pharmacovigilance in Rare Myopathies
blogs.description: An overview of the WHO‑Uppsala monitoring framework, how clinicians can report suspected adverse effects, and why early reporting of GLP‑1 receptor agonist‑related muscle toxicity matters for product labels, prescribing guidelines, and future research.
